chunks: Wahb ibn Wahb al-Qurashi said: Zayd ibn Ali Zayn al-Abidin (peace be upon him) said:

Al-Samad is He who, when He intends a thing, says to it: 'Be!' and it is. Al-Samad is He who originated the things, creating them as opposites, forms, and pairs. He is Unique in Oneness, without opposite, form, likeness, or equal.

key_terms.الصَّمَدُ: Al-Samad (The Absolute, The One who is self-sufficient and to whom all refer)

ai.seo_question: What does the title 'Al-Samad' mean in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Zayd ibn Ali, a prominent figure in early Shia scholarship, links the title 'Al-Samad' to both divine creative power and absolute ontological uniqueness, emphasizing that God’s command ('Be') brings forth creation in diverse pairs while remaining distinct from them. This interpretation aligns with the Shia emphasis on Tawhid al-Dhat (Unity of Essence), distinguishing God’s essence from His attributes and creations. The hadith reinforces the concept of God’s self-sufficiency and transcendence, central to Surah Al-Ikhlas.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 4. Wahab ibn Wahab al-Qarashi related that Zayd ibn `Ali Zayn al-`Abidin (AS) said: “

When the Needless [al-Samad] intends a thing, He says: `Be!’ and it is. The Needless orginaters all thing, crates them in contrast, similarity, and pairs. He is Unique in Oneness, without opposite, similarity, likeness, or equal.”
